episode_title: Build the Business BEFORE You Buy Real Estate

real_qa.q: How should real estate investors build the business before buying properties?
real_qa.r: Build the entire business first by hiring experts such as property managers, contractors, plumbers, roofers, inspectors, and mortgage workers before purchasing any real estate. Contact property managers in advance to determine rental rates, vacancy factors, and whether they will manage the property. Calculate all expenses including mortgage, taxes, insurance, vacancy factor, and repairs to determine required rental income, then only purchase if the property meets your cash flow target.
real_qa.requete: build business before buying real estate

real_qa.q: What minimum monthly cash flow does Dustin Heiner require for long-term rental properties?
real_qa.r: Dustin Heiner does not buy a property unless it makes at least $500 a month in cash flow after all expenses including the property manager. With multiple properties generating $500 monthly, he demonstrates that 20 properties at $500 per month equals $10,000 monthly or $120,000 annually, and some of his properties generate as much as $3,000 a month in cash flow.

real_qa.q: Why did Dustin Heiner leave his government job despite having job security?
real_qa.r: Dustin Heiner was laid off from his county government job in California on a Friday at 3:30 p.m. after returning from paternity leave, despite believing he had a secure position. This experience taught him that he could not rely on employment for financial security and made him realize he needed to build wealth through real estate and business ownership so that nobody could take away his ability to provide for his family.

real_qa.q: What is Dustin Heiner's approach to acquiring undervalued properties using multiple offers?
real_qa.r: Dustin Heiner's team submits 50 offers per week because they have no way of knowing which sellers will accept an offer that fits their investment criteria. One of his students purchased a probate property in Birmingham, Alabama listed for $181,000 but got it under contract for $121,000, then negotiated a $20,000 repair credit from the seller, resulting in a total purchase price of $99,000 for a property worth $200,000 after repairs with $700 monthly cash flow.
real_qa.requete: 50 offers per week real estate deals

real_qa.q: How did Dustin Heiner transition from passive income to meaningful work that fulfills him?
real_qa.r: After quitting his job in 2016, Dustin Heiner played golf and went to movies for about a month but became bored with pure leisure. He then realized he is driven by people, not money, and changed his goal from making a million dollars in annual profit to focusing on real estate and business as vehicles for helping people, understanding that real estate is about people and business is about people, not just properties or products.
real_qa.requete: financially independent what to do next
